paper.title: Online Learning to Rank in Stochastic Click Models

unmapped: Actions are ordered lists of K distinct items out of L (ranking); reward = number of clicks
Feedback: click indicators on each position, where click = examination indicator x attraction indicator; attraction of unexamined items is not observed (partial-monitoring-like click feedback)

Click model: independent Bernoulli attractions; examination probabilities general (covers cascade and position-based models) subject to order-independent, decreasing, correct-scaling and optimal examination assumptions (Assumptions 1-6)
Optimal list unique as a set
settings.definition_quote: We refer to our learning problem as a \emph{stochastic click bandit}. An instance of this problem is a tuple $(K, L, P_\attrprob, P_\examprob)$, where $K$ is the number of positions, $L$ is the number of items, $P_\attrprob$ is a distribution over binary vectors $\set{0, 1}^L$, and $P_\examprob$ is a distribution over binary matrices

bound.expression_latex: \frac{192 K^3 L}{(1 - \attrprob_{\max}) \Delta_{\min}} \log T + 4 K L (3 e + K)

symbols.m: number of positions K in the ranked list (paper's K)
symbols.Delta_min_att: min_{k in [K]} (alpha(k) - alpha(k+1)), gap between consecutive attraction probabilities among the top K+1 items

conditions: Assumptions 1-6 (independent attractions, attraction-examination independence, order-independent, decreasing, correct-scaling and optimal examination)
optimal list unique as a set
tuning: delta_T = log T + 3 log log T

source.label: thm:upper bound
source.quote: For any stochastic click bandit in \cref{sec:stochastic click bandit} that satisfies Assumptions \ref{ass:attraction independence} to \ref{ass:optimal examination} and $T \geq 5$, the expected $T$-step regret of $\mergerank$ is bounded as R(T) \leq \frac{192 K^3 L}{(1 - \attrprob_{\max}) \Delta_{\min}} \log T + 4 K L (3 e + K), where $\Delta_{\min} = \min_{k \in [K]} \set{\attrprob(k) - \attrprob(k + 1)}$.

results.notes: Regret is E of reward difference vs optimal list with shared randomness, equal to expected-reward gap, hence pseudo-regret. Paper's K (positions) renamed m; L (items) renamed L_items. Algorithm uses T in its stage lengths and confidence bounds.

cited_results.setting_description: Learning the most clicked item-position pair in a specific PBM (first position examined w.p. ~1, others ~0), solved as a stochastic rank-1 bandit; mu = O(1/K)
